newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S. Korean minister says economy in serious trouble.
newsitem.headline: S. Korean minister says economy in serious trouble.

text.p: Finance minister Kang Kyong-shik said on Thursday that South Korea's economy was in serious trouble, battered by bankruptcies, a month of labour strikes and a political crisis.
"There is no doubt the Korean economy is currently in serious trouble," he told a news conference.
Kang said the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co in January, labour unrest and a related political crisis had "all added more uncertainties and instability in the economy".

He said much of South Korea's current account deficit was due to a sharp downturn in the terms of trade, fuelled by plunging prices of exports, including semiconductors. The deficit hit an all-time high of $23.72 billion last year.
"The fear is that there may be a further decline in the balance of payments as the economy's structural problems take a toll on the country's international competitiveness," Kang said.
